questiontext.text:
Arrange the following tissue layers of a primary dicotyledonous root in the correct sequence from the outermost surface towards the centre:

  • (P) Cortex
  • (Q) Epiblema
  • (R) Pericycle
  • (S) Endodermis

Select the correct order from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a transverse section of a primary dicotyledonous root, tissues are arranged concentrically from the outermost protective layer inward towards the central stele.

Step 2: Evaluation of Spatial Order
1. The outermost layer of the dicotyledonous root is the epiblema, from which unicellular root hairs protrude.
2. Inner to the epiblema lies the cortex, consisting of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells with intercellular spaces.
3. The innermost layer of the cortex is the endodermis, a single layer of barrel-shaped cells bearing casparian strips.
4. Next to the endodermis, forming the outermost boundary of the stele, lies the pericycle consisting of thick-walled parenchymatous cells.

Step 3: Verification of Sequence
Tracing from the outside inward yields the sequence: Epiblema (Q), followed by Cortex (P), followed by Endodermis (S), and then Pericycle (R).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence from the outermost surface towards the centre is Q, P, S, R.

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events of vascular cambium formation and activity during secondary growth in a dicotyledonous stem in the correct chronological sequence:

  • (P) Medullary ray cells adjoining intrafascicular cambium become meristematic to form interfascicular cambium
  • (Q) The continuous cambial ring cuts off secondary xylem towards the pith and secondary phloem towards the periphery
  • (R) Intrafascicular cambium is present in patches between primary xylem and primary phloem
  • (S) Primary and secondary phloems get gradually crushed due to continued accumulation of secondary xylem

Select the correct chronological order from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Secondary growth in girth of a dicotyledonous stem begins with the completion of a continuous vascular cambium ring, followed by its unequal bidirectional meristematic activity.

Step 2: Evaluation of Chronological Stages
1. Initially, in the young dicot stem, vascular cambium is present only in patches between primary xylem and primary phloem as intrafascicular cambium (R).
2. Next, the cells of the medullary rays adjoining these intrafascicular cambium strips become meristematic and form the interfascicular cambium, uniting the patches into a continuous cambial ring (P).
3. Once formed, the cambial ring becomes active and cuts off new cells towards both sides—maturing into secondary xylem towards the pith and secondary phloem towards the periphery (Q).
4. Because the cambium is more active on the inner side, a large compact mass of secondary xylem accumulates, which gradually crushes the primary and secondary phloems towards the outside (S).

Step 3: Verification of Sequence
The logical and developmental progression is R, followed by P, followed by Q, and finally S.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence of events is R, P, Q, S.

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events associated with cork cambium (phellogen) and periderm formation in a dicotyledonous stem in the correct chronological sequence:

  • (P) Another meristematic tissue called cork cambium (phellogen) develops in the cortex region
  • (Q) Outer cortical and epidermis layers get broken due to increase in girth caused by vascular cambium activity
  • (R) Phellogen cuts off outer cells differentiating into cork (phellem) and inner cells differentiating into secondary cortex (phelloderm)
  • (S) Pressure builds up on the remaining layers peripheral to phellogen, causing them to die and slough off

Select the correct chronological order from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Periderm formation is a protective secondary response triggered when primary outer tissues rupture due to internal expansion from vascular cambium activity.

Step 2: Evaluation of Chronological Stages
1. As the stem continues to increase in girth due to the activity of the vascular cambium, the outer cortical and epidermis layers get broken and need replacement (Q).
2. To provide new protective cell layers, cork cambium (phellogen) develops, usually in the cortex region (P).
3. Phellogen divides to cut off cells on both sides: the outer cells differentiate into suberised cork (phellem) and the inner cells differentiate into parenchymatous secondary cortex (phelloderm) (R).
4. Due to the continued activity of the cork cambium, pressure builds up on the remaining layers peripheral to phellogen, and ultimately these layers die and slough off (S).

Step 3: Verification of Sequence
The causal and chronological progression is Q, followed by P, followed by R, and finally S.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence of events is Q, P, R, S.
